items.action: Only if you wrote a workaround: a rule that killed one of the two rings — `box-shadow: none` on an inner input, or a re-declared `--ds-input-focus-shadow` meant to hide the doubling — can go.
items.appliesWhen: Deliberately NOT suppressed: the clear button and the password toggle inside the same box keep their own ring, because both are real tab stops the box halo cannot distinguish.
items.note: The two shells 0.10.2's pass missed. A focused ds-input or ds-textarea drew the 4px control ring the universal `:where(:focus-visible)` rule puts on the inner element, plus the 3px field halo the box paints on `:focus-within`. The inner one is suppressed now.
items.verify: Tab into a ds-input and a ds-textarea: each shows exactly one ring, the halo around the box. Tab on to the clear button or password toggle inside that field and a second, tighter ring appears on the button - that one is intended.

items.action: Only if you re-added a ring to that button yourself — that rule can go. (delete list: search-clear-button-focus-rule)
items.note: 0.10.2's ring fix silenced the base indicator with a shell-wide reset, which also hit `.search-clear`, a `tabindex=0` tab stop: in every shadow-based focus style, tabbing from the input to the clear button changed nothing on screen — box-shadow, outline, border, background and colour all identical (only `data-focus="outline"` and forced colours still drew an outline) — so a keyboard user could not tell it had focus. A WCAG 2.4.7 failure. Every shell names the single control it silences now.
items.verify: Type into a ds-search so the clear button appears, then Tab: the × shows its own ring on top of the field halo. Same for a chip close button in ds-autocomplete or ds-multi-select, and for the arrows in ds-number-stepper.

items.action: Only if you worked around either: a rule adding a ring to `.period-trigger`, `.picker-cell`, `.preset-btn` or `.time-action`, or a `border-radius` forced onto `.time-panel`, can go.
items.pitfall: The mechanism is worth knowing before you style a DS panel yourself: a private `--_*` token declared on `:host` does NOT reach a panel the CDK has portaled out of that host, and an unresolvable `var()` silently becomes the property's initial value — `none` for box-shadow, `0` for border-radius. Read the PUBLIC `--ds-*` token from outside instead.
items.note: Tabbable buttons inside both portaled panels had no focus indicator at all - the date-picker's month/year header, month and year cells and preset buttons, and the time-picker's action button - and one panel had square corners: all read a private focus-shadow token declared on the host, and with `outline: none` beside it nothing was left.
items.verify: Open the ds-date-picker calendar and Tab to the month/year header, a month or year cell and a preset button: each shows a focus ring. Open the ds-time-picker panel and Tab to its action button: same. The time-picker panel has rounded corners.

informational: If you add a component that paints its own ring on :focus-within, suppress the base rule on the control it speaks for - `outline: 0` cannot do it, because the base indicator is a box-shadow.

Two authoring mixins are now documented for consumers building their own composite controls: `focus.owns-the-focus-ring($control)` in styles/focus, and `text-clip.single-line-ellipsis` in styles/text-clip. Both are opt-in - no existing code changes.

A private --_* token declared on :host does not reach a CDK-portaled panel, and an unresolvable var() silently becomes the property's initial value - none for box-shadow, 0 for border-radius. If you style a DS panel from your own CSS, read the PUBLIC --ds-* token there, not the private one.

Fourteen public tokens were always overridable but never reached the token reference: --ds-container-pad-x, --ds-multi-select-border-color (+-focus), --ds-segmented-selected-bg-color / -label-color / --ds-segmented-radius, --ds-time-picker-option-bg-color-selected / -text-color-selected / -bg-color-hover, --ds-time-picker-trigger-bg-color / -border / -color, --ds-field-message-icon-offset, --ds-time-picker-focus-shadow (it reaches the time-picker panel's action button only from this release - see portaled-panel-focus-indicator). Otherwise nothing changed in the components - if you hand-rolled around one of these because it looked unsupported, the override is supported and is the way to do it.

deleteList.why: A rule killing one of the two focus rings a ds-input or ds-textarea used to paint - typically box-shadow: none on the inner input, or --ds-input-focus-shadow re-declared as none to hide the doubling.
deleteList.replaceWith: nothing - the component now paints one ring on its own

deleteList.why: A focus rule you added to the ds-search clear button because it showed no indicator at all - the shell-wide reset 0.10.2 used silenced that tab stop too. Every shell names the one control it silences now, so the button keeps its own ring.
